title: Life before the army, sports and what pleased him
summary: His life then was not all music; he loved sports and weighed ball playing against music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: I'm curious, your life had been--up to that moment--nothing but music and your associations were nothing but musicians and you had, I would assume, very little in common with the litter bearers, do you see what I'm getting at?
Why you didn't want to rush back into your own milieu.

This is 1942 and I'm twenty two years old. I came back to music when I was about fifteen, I guess and for a few years it was nothing but kids and kid bands and learning and listening, so I wasn't really that full of music and musical friends and musical life. As a matter of fact, there was very little of it

up to that point. I had made some contacts, some friends, I had done a little musical work, but I wasn't that full of it so that I could have said my life up to that point had been nothing but music. I spent more time I guess up to then, playing ball than I did anything else. That was my love.
Did you ever think that you might become a professional ballplayer?
Yes. I had to make a decision whether to go out for sports or go out for music.
I think so. I think I would have done probably best in football, although I was a good baseball player. I was probably championship caliber in swimmer--I was a speed swimmer. That's it.
(Side A of Tape 2 ended at this point. Transcript will continue in accordance with Side B.)
If circumstances had brushed you against a scout for the Cardinals or for the New York Giants, would you have been perfectly happy to have been plucked out of this and become a ball player?

Well, I don't know, it would have depended on what was offered to me and whether it would have affected me. If they had offered what I thought would have been a lot of money, I might have done it, because at that time of my life there were three things that gave me pleasure, music, sports and sex.
You can't make much money in sex, so that would be--
No. You could but not me. I was not the gigolo, whoreish type.
